Delta self-reference hole: changes to `architect_review.py`/`precheck.py` themselves are "unchanged context" under a delta review; no rule forces full re-review when review tooling or gate config changes.

Reversibility claim conflicts with AC4: "store/registry/doc updates included" implies persisted state (last_reviewed_HEAD, prior dispositions), but rollback says "no persisted state migration" — revert path for stored review state is undefined.
Enforced-item list duplicated between `config/design-pack.json`, `gate1_check.py`, and `precheck.py` with no stated single source of truth — drift will silently weaken the gate.

MINOR: No observability plan: gate/design-pack/encoding failures emit no structured reason codes or metrics, hindering diagnosis of recurring blocker classes (CL-009).
Data-only-commit rule ("does not invalidate the review") has no stated precedence logic relative to concurrent tooling commits — ordering ambiguity.
Rollback does not cover partial failure of design-pack generation (template written, config not) leaving `engineering/design/<ID>.md` orphaned.
Delta risk mitigation relies on "first full review" with no defined cadence or trigger for periodic full re-baseline.

SUMMARY: Verdict: not ready for Gate 1.5; the design restates ACs without mechanisms for evidence binding, delta re-baseline, or test coverage, and leaves the guardrail checklist undispositioned.

Top risks: (1) unbound review evidence makes delta reviews non-auditable, (2) CL-006/CL-008 non-compliance invalidates approval, (3) divergence between duplicated enforced-item definitions silently weakens gates.
Direction is sound (tooling-only, Python-OK, reversible, no 1484 coupling); needs concrete base/head persistence design, self-reference rule, and explicit guardrail answers before proceeding.
